paper.title: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
paper.central_claim: A pixel-only agent with generic mouse/keyboard actions, Pix2Struct initialization and tree-search policy improvement outperforms human crowdworkers on MiniWob++, with an initial pixel-only WebShop baseline.

evidence.quote: its performance drops by 75% when the DOM information is removed from the agent’s observations.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors locate a concrete observation bottleneck in CC-Net; this is an attributed baseline report, not independently inspected CC-Net original.

evidence.quote: Importantly, the DOM information is not provided by the environment and is therefore not used in any way to define observations or actions.
evidence.support_explanation: Inference uses screenshots and generic coordinates; pretraining and demonstration conversion still use HTML-derived supervision.

evidence.quote: For each task, we compute the mean over 100 random seeds, and then compute the mean over 59 MiniWob++ tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Defines the measurement denominator and that reward may be partial rather than binary success.
Policy weights retain search-generated improvements across subsequently evaluated seeds, not search at final inference.

evidence.quote: pre-training improves task scores from 17.1 to 66.5 on MiniWob++ and from 1.1 to 46.7 on WebShop.
evidence.support_explanation: Within-recipe pretraining ablation supports transfer of screenshot parsing.

evidence.quote: we estimate the performance of CC-Net without DOM information by assuming that the drop in performance on the subset of tasks we study was also 75%.
evidence.support_explanation: Fourfold comparator is estimated, not a matched rerun.

evidence.quote: Pix2Act can reach a mean score of 28.3 on held out tasks compared to 65.5 when training on those tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Nontrivial heldout-task generalization is far from solving the generalization problem; manually chosen tasks.

evidence.quote: We evaluated on 59 of these 104 tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Scope excludes scrolling, animations, copy/paste and unsupported Selenium interaction; selection is stated to be conversion-based, not performance-based.

evidence.quote: We then filter trajectories where the raw reward is < 0.8 <0.8 .
evidence.support_explanation: Execution reward gates model-generated trajectories; supervised updates, fixed value net, two iterations.
MCTS 16 traversals, top-8 actions, rollout max20, lambda0.1; 64 TPU v3 cores but no total walltime or cost-matched PPO/search comparison.

evidence.quote: the standard deviation across these trials was 0.15 0.15
evidence.support_explanation: Three evaluation-seed trials 96.2/96.4/96.1; not three independently trained models.

signatures.information: Screenshot with rendered instruction/cursor/button state; WebShop last5 actions rendered. No inference DOM. HTML-derived pretraining and demo conversion are training privileges.
signatures.operation: Convert X11/high-level demonstrations into generic discretized click/drag/type/scroll tokens; fine-tune Pix2Struct end-to-end.
signatures.conditions: Selenium-supported actions; adequate visual resolution; inherited screenshot parsing pretraining.
signatures.feedback: Human demonstrations and per-benchmark execution rewards.
signatures.selection_rule: Drop demonstration raw reward<0.8; conversion must succeed.
signatures.selection_data: ~1.3M source MiniWoB demos, 6% reward-filtered, 81% of remainder converted; 10% development. WebShop1012/54/500.
signatures.persistence: Fine-tuned model parameters; within-episode action-per-observation cache prevents exact cycles.
signatures.later_use: Greedy action selection on heldout seeds/instructions.
signatures.claimed_effect: BC66.5 vs17.1 without pretraining; WebShop46.7 vs1.1.
signatures.failure_boundary: 59/104 tasks; coordinate discretization and unsupported real-time/scroll/copy actions; WebShop below HTML models.

signatures.object: BC policy -> MCTS-generated expert corpus -> updated policy
signatures.information: Training has resettable deterministic simulator and terminal reward; final greedy deployment does not search or access reward.
signatures.operation: Search top8 actions, 16 MCTS rounds; combine fixed value net and max20-step policy rollouts; filter successful episodes then SFT; repeat twice.
signatures.output: 826K search trajectories and updated policy parameters
signatures.conditions: Resettable procedural task seeds, reward checker, search support.
signatures.feedback: Raw execution reward plus -1/30 step penalty; lambda0.1 value/rollout mixture.
signatures.selection_rule: Keep raw reward>=0.8; MCTS chooses most-visited action.
signatures.selection_data: Fresh sampled training tasks/seeds; search hyperparameters minimally tuned; exact seed disjointness not enumerated.
signatures.persistence: Policy theta updated by SFT; value phi fixed.
signatures.later_use: Greedy scores on subsequent evaluation seeds66.5->93.1->96.2.
signatures.claimed_effect: Retained trained-policy improvement, not improved learning algorithm across independently heldout domains.
signatures.failure_boundary: No equal-training-compute BC/PPO control; reward/reset assumptions; limited OOD evaluation.
